walkthroughs.body_html:
International Trade and the Global Economy — a core area of GCSE Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

International Trade and the Global Economy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with International Trade and the Global Economy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Specialisation based on lowest opportunity cost is:
options: Absolute advantage
Comparative advantage
Free trade
Protectionism

mcqs.q: A tariff is a tax on:
options: Exports
Imports
Domestic production
Consumption

mcqs.q: What does standard theory predict about a minimum wage?
options: Higher interest rates make money more valuable so inflation falls automatically.
If above equilibrium, it raises wages for those still employed but causes unemployment by reducing labour demand — though empirical evidence is mixed.
A minimum wage is paid by the government.
A minimum wage always reduces unemployment because workers have more money to spend.

mcqs.q: Is a trade deficit necessarily bad?
options: A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
A trade deficit always means a country is losing wealth and failing economically.
Not necessarily — it can reflect strong domestic demand, attractive investment opportunities, or borrowing to fund growth. Context matters more than the headline figure.
Higher interest rates make money more valuable so inflation falls automatically.

mcqs.q: How does raising interest rates reduce inflation?
options: Higher interest rates make money more valuable so inflation falls automatically.
Higher rates make borrowing more expensive and saving more attractive, reducing consumption and investment — lowering aggregate demand and slowing price rises.
Higher interest rates directly force shops to lower their prices.
A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
